answer: A farm that wants 143 keys as a result burns 143 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the nebula seed, the meadow timing is verifiable from the shale record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 260 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
